summary: A generated brief can formalize the wrong problem, add process overhead, or create false agreement.

points.text: When the requester lacks domain knowledge, review may become rubber-stamping: the same person who supplied an underspecified prompt may be unable to detect the model's invented business rule.
For a tiny, reversible change, producing and approving a full task contract can cost more than implementation and direct review.
The model can anchor the conversation around its first decomposition. Stakeholders may edit wording while failing to reconsider a missing alternative or an incorrect problem frame.
Sensitive issue context may be copied into an external service. Mediation adds another data boundary that needs retention, access, and provider controls.
